web_text_verbatim: Classification of scapular body fractures based on anatomical location (Infraspinous Fossa, Scapular Spine, Medial/Lateral Border). Ada-Miller categorization includes processes (I), neck (II), glenoid (III), and body (IV).
quote: Ada–Miller classification of scapular fractures is as follows: IA, acromion fractures; IB, scapular spine fractures; IC, coracoid process fractures; IIA, “fractures of the surgical neck”; IIB, “trans-spinous fractures of the neck”; IIC, “fractures of the neck inferior to the scapular spine”; III, fractures of the glenoid; and IV, fractures of the body.

web_text_verbatim: Glenopolar Angle (GPA) <22° (or <=20°) indicates severe angular deformity / rotational malalignment with poor functional outcomes.

quote: The GPA is defined as an acute angle between the line connecting the superior and inferior poles of glenoid and the line connecting the superior pole of glenoid with the inferior angle of scapula (Fig. 33-7).33 According to Tuček et al.,213 the standard GPA value in the Neer I view is 41 degrees (range 35–51 degrees).

web_text_verbatim: SSSC (Superior Shoulder Suspensory Complex) represents a bone-soft tissue ring (glenoid, coracoid, CC ligaments, clavicle, AC joint, acromion). Double disruption creates a floating shoulder.

quote: defined it as an osseofibrous ring formed by the glenoid, coracoid, CC ligament, lateral clavicle, AC joint, AC ligament

web_text_verbatim: Ideberg classification modified by Goss categorizes glenoid fractures into rim fractures (Type I) and central glenoid fossa fractures (Types II to VI).
quote: He recognized two main groups of fractures, that is, glenoid rim fractures, or type I, and central fractures of the glenoid fossa, types II to VI

ui_location: Glenoid > การจัดจำแนก > Ideberg (Goss Modification) > ข้อบ่งชี้/เกณฑ์ตัดสินใจ (The Rules)
web_text_verbatim: Intra-articular displacement or step-off >=2-4 mm or joint subluxation warrants operative anatomical reduction and rigid fixation.
focus: Glenoid articular step-off threshold for surgery
quote: Glenoid fractures should be treated as all other intraarticular fractures, and reduced and stabilized when signiﬁcant (>4 mm) displacement exists through the articular surface that leads to joint subluxation or incongruency.

ui_location: Acromion > การจัดจำแนก > Kuhn > ภาพรวม
web_text_verbatim: Kuhn acromion classification: Type I (non-displaced), Type II (displaced without reduction of subacromial space), Type III (displaced with reduction of subacromial space causing impingement).
focus: Kuhn acromion classification and subacromial impingement
quote: Angulated nonunions of the lateral spine may compromise the subacromial space and cause impingement

ui_location: Coracoid > การจัดจำแนก > Ogawa > ภาพรวม
web_text_verbatim: Ogawa coracoid classification: Type I (proximal to CC ligament attachment, unstable, frequently associated with superior glenoid or SSSC injury) vs Type II (distal to CC ligament, stable).
quote: Ogawa et al.165 evaluated the results of operative treatment in 36 patients with a coracoid fracture of Ogawa type I. In 12 patients, the fracture line involved the superior glenoid fossa.

ui_location: Coracoid > การจัดจำแนก > Eyres > ภาพรวม
web_text_verbatim: Eyres coracoid classification: Types I-V according to anatomical level from tip/apex (Type I) down to base and intra-articular glenoid extension (Type V).
quote: The study group comprised 12 intra-articular coracoid base fractures of Eyres type V.

web_text_verbatim: Scapulothoracic dissociation (STD) represents a closed internal amputation of the shoulder girdle caused by massive violent traction force, with lateral scapular displacement >1 cm on chest radiograph and high mortality (~11%).
quote: STD is a rare, severe, high-energy injury characterized by disconnection of the osseoligamentous system of the scapula from the axial skeleton at various levels

web_text_verbatim: Zelle / Damschen classification categorizes severity: Type 1 musculoskeletal disruption alone, Type 2 incomplete brachial plexus injury, Type 3 vascular transection, Type 4 complete brachial plexus avulsion (poor prognosis, consider primary amputation).
